definition.title: Compare outcomes under uncertainty
definition.description: Compare separate nonfinancial outcomes using supplied response ranges, explicit goals and priorities. Preserve unresolved choices, evidence applicability, sensitivity and progress measures.

definition.title: Compare outcomes under uncertainty
definition.responsibility: Compare supplied outcome ranges and explicit priorities, expose unresolved tradeoffs, and define observations that could change the choice.
invariants: Outcome units and directions remain separate; no combined score or implicit monetary value is inferred.
Ranges are supplied assumptions, not confidence intervals, causal effects, or predicted individual responses.
Missing estimates and uncertain applicability remain unknown and never become zero or a reason to prefer another option by absence.
A robust preference requires conservative interval separation at the first priority that differs; overlapping priority ranges cannot be bypassed.
Declared targets express aspirations, not clinical suitability, observed success, or authorization.
Sensitivity scenarios compare declared assumptions; they do not estimate probabilities or discover new evidence.

caseDerivation: Alternative identities and separate outcome units, directions and bounds remain frozen.
Case workers supply explicit estimate ranges and source applicability judgments; missing or unsupported estimates remain unknown.
Explicit priorities and aspirations define the conditional comparison; no implicit weights, money conversion or causal effects are inferred.

app.name: Compare learning-support plans
app.description: Compare the next six-week support block for a fictional eight-year-old whose dyslexia and ADHD have already been professionally assessed. A positive classroom report can coexist with persistent decoding difficulty; renewing support on one overall success judgment could leave another need insufficiently addressed. Every response range is an authored assumption, not a validated prediction or a confidence interval. The classroom package is support for attention-related difficulties, not a complete clinical ADHD treatment. Separate progress measures inform reconsideration; before-and-after change alone does not establish a causal effect.

alternatives.label: Targeted word-reading support
alternatives.description: A complete word-reading support package for this comparison. Its assumed decoding benefit does not automatically establish improvement in attention-related classroom difficulties.

alternatives.label: Classroom support for attention-related difficulties
alternatives.description: A complete classroom-support package for this comparison, not a complete clinical ADHD treatment. Completing more work is not treated as evidence of better word decoding.

alternatives.label: Coordinated support
alternatives.description: A coordinated package addressing both recorded needs, with greater weekly burden. It is not assumed to dominate the focused alternatives.

outcomes.label: Word-reading improvement
outcomes.unit: change in correct items on a fixed 20-item decoding probe
outcomes.description: Change from this fictional case’s baseline of 6 correct items out of 20. Negative change remains possible. The fixed baseline defines the permitted change range; another baseline requires an adapted model. It is separate from work completed.

outcomes.label: Classroom-participation improvement
outcomes.unit: percentage-point change in engaged observation intervals
outcomes.description: Change from this fictional case’s baseline of 45% under a fixed classroom observation protocol. Negative change remains possible. It is not an ADHD diagnosis or a measure of decoding.

outcomes.label: Additional weekly burden
outcomes.description: Additional practice and coordination time borne by the child and family. It is kept separate from improvement rather than converted into money.

assumptions: Dyslexia and ADHD have already been professionally assessed in this fictional case; the calculation does not diagnose them or determine clinical suitability.

The decision concerns the next six-week support block. Better classroom participation does not by itself establish that the decoding need is sufficiently addressed; decoding improvement does not by itself establish adequate classroom functioning.

All alternatives are complete authored support descriptions for this bounded comparison. Classroom support for attention-related difficulties is not a complete clinical ADHD treatment. The range comparison does not prescribe medication, infer clinical efficacy or produce a probability of benefit.
Targets and priority order are explicit human judgments. A preferred option is conditional on supplied estimates, applicability and preferences; overlapping ranges can leave the choice unresolved.
The six-week horizon and baseline values are fictional teaching inputs. Qualified professionals must choose appropriate measures and reconsideration criteria.

case.title: Fictional support comparison for Sam, age eight
case.scope: Sam is a fictional eight-year-old whose dyslexia and ADHD have already been professionally assessed. Elena, the support coordinator, is helping the child, family and professionals choose his next six-week support block. His teacher sees improved participation while unfamiliar words remain difficult to decode. A single reassuring “working” judgment could renew a plan without addressing that remaining difficulty. The comparison keeps both needs and the child’s and family’s burden visible. monitoring.measure: Baseline: 6 correct items on the declared 20-item unfamiliar-word probe. Record correct items on comparable probes using the same scoring protocol; a qualified professional determines an appropriate measure.
monitoring.when: Baseline before support, weekly observations, and a six-week reconsideration point.
monitoring.interpretation: Reconsider the assumed reading benefit if observed change fails to approach the agreed four-item goal or the measure is not suitable. Improvement in participation cannot substitute. Repeated measurements alone do not establish treatment causality.

monitoring.measure: Baseline: engaged in 45% of fixed classroom observation intervals. Record engagement under a declared observation protocol, with lesson and observer context.
monitoring.when: Baseline before support, weekly observations, and a six-week reconsideration point.
monitoring.interpretation: Reconsider the assumed participation benefit if change does not approach the agreed eight-percentage-point goal, contexts differ, or observations conflict. Do not infer decoding improvement or a diagnosis from engagement.

monitoring.measure: Baseline: zero additional minutes attributable to the proposed package. Record actual additional child and family practice and coordination time.
monitoring.when: Record weekly, including incomplete sessions and family feedback; reconsider at six weeks or earlier if burden is unacceptable.
monitoring.interpretation: Reconsider the package if actual burden exceeds the accepted bound or the child or family finds it unacceptable, even when another outcome improves. These observations do not measure efficacy.
